angle: Nostalgia: Maa's recipe (“a pinch of this, cook till done”) works for family who already know the dish. AI is a stranger in your kitchen, so it needs the full recipe card. Proof is a real test scenario (dinner for 2 vegetarians, no oven), run twice per prompt, never the creator's own diet or kitchen.

slides.headline: You prompt AI like Maa writes recipes
slides.body: “A pinch of this, cook till done.” Works for family. In my test, AI guessed chicken for two vegetarians.

An arrow runs from the diary page to a chat-box doodle, and out of the chat box comes a small chicken-leg doodle with a question mark. Handwritten hook above. A small “swipe →” arrow in the bottom corner.

slides.headline: AI is a stranger in your kitchen
slides.body: Family knows the dish. AI has to guess. It said so itself: “If you tell me … what's in your fridge, I can tailor it.”
slides.visual: Frame 0 shows the headline. Calm draw-on, about 7 s: a kitchen doorway in line art, then a small friendly robot standing at the door holding an empty plate with a question mark above it. A speech bubble draws out from the robot as a typewriter quote card holding the trimmed line. A pencil tag above the card reads “after a vague prompt”, and a tiny label under it reads “real run, trimmed”. Yellow highlighter sweeps over “stranger” and then “what's in your fridge” last.

slides.headline: A pinch of prompt. A stranger's dinner.
slides.body: The test: dinner for 2 vegetarians, no oven. The prompt never said so. Run 1 served: “Lemon-Garlic Chicken …” “Heat the oven to 220°C …”
slides.visual: Left: a sticky note with the prompt in handwriting: “Give me a healthy dinner recipe”. An arrow leads to a paper card holding the two trimmed output quotes in typewriter text, with a small oven doodle and a chicken-leg doodle. A tiny label on the card corner: “real run, trimmed”. Yellow highlighter on “Chicken” and “oven”. A margin note in pencil: “both runs: chicken, quinoa, oven at 220°C”.

slides.headline: So I wrote it a recipe card
slides.body: Same model, same dinner test. This time the prompt had six labelled lines. Next slide: what came back.
slides.visual: Frame 0 shows the headline and an empty ruled index card. Calm draw-on, about 7 s: only six short rows write themselves down the card, one by one, three or four words each: “Serves: who it's for” / “Ingredients: what you have” / “Method: the answer's shape” / “Tastes like: one example” / “Don't: your limits” / “Taste and adjust: self-check”. No full prompt lines here. Yellow highlighter lands on the six labels at the end. A small arrow at the bottom right points to the next slide.

slides.headline: Same AI, cooking for the kitchen I described
slides.body: “Palak paneer moong dal (serves 2, about 25 minutes)” … “Paneer: 200 g” … “about 34 g per serving” (AI's estimate, not verified nutrition). No oven.
slides.visual: A paper card with the trimmed output quotes in typewriter text beside a hand-drawn bowl of dal with paneer cubes and a spinach leaf. A tiny label on the card corner: “real run, trimmed”. A crossed-out oven doodle in the corner. A sticky note pointing at the protein figure reads “AI's estimate”. Yellow highlighter on “Palak paneer moong dal” and “200 g”. A pencil margin note: “second run: paneer-palak moong dal tadka, about 27 minutes”. A small arrow at the bottom right: “the six lines →”.

slides.headline: First, tell the stranger who's eating
slides.body: Serves: who it's for. Ingredients: what you have. The test card: “2 people, vegetarian, about 30 g protein each” … “No oven.”
slides.visual: Two sticky notes side by side. Left note “Serves” with two stick figures at a small table. Right note “Ingredients” with an open kitchen shelf in line art: paneer block, dal jar, onion, tomato, spinach, curd bowl, and a crossed-out oven. Under the notes, a thin typewriter strip with the trimmed prompt quotes and a tiny label: “real run, trimmed”. Arrows from both notes point to the robot from slide 2, now one step inside the door and holding a notepad. Yellow highlighter on “who it's for” and “what you have”.

slides.headline: Show it what “done” looks like
slides.body: Method: the answer's shape. Tastes like: one example. Back came: “Start the dal (18 minutes). Rinse the 100 g moong dal …”

On the right, a steaming bowl draws in with a tadka ladle above it, labelled with the prompt line “Tastes like: dal tadka, but lighter.” Then a typewriter quote card draws in along the bottom with the trimmed output step, and a tiny label on its corner: “real run, trimmed”. Yellow highlighter lands on “18 minutes” and “100 g” last.

slides.headline: Maa tastes before serving. So should AI.
slides.body: Don't: limits. Taste and adjust: self-check, plus one question. It asked: “Will you eat this on its own, or with rice or roti?”
slides.visual: Left: a sticky note “Don't” with three small crossed-out doodles: a frying kadhai, a cream carton, a clock past 30. Right: a hand holding a tasting spoon over a pot, labelled “Taste and adjust”, with a small typewriter line beside the spoon: “about 34 g per serving, so it clears the 30 g goal” and a pencil tag “AI's estimate”. Below, a speech bubble from the robot with the verbatim question. A tiny label under the bubble: “real run, trimmed”. Yellow highlighter on “self-check” and “one question”.

slides.headline: Save this: the six-line recipe card
slides.body: Serves: who it's for. Ingredients: what you have. Method: answer shape. Tastes like: one example. Don't: limits. Taste and adjust: self-check, one question.

caption:
You prompt AI the way Maa writes recipes: “a pinch of this, cook till done”.

That works for family, because they have eaten the dish a hundred times. AI has never eaten at your table. It is a stranger in your kitchen.

So I tested it. Same model, same day, each prompt run twice. The test scenario: dinner for 2 vegetarians, no oven. Prompt 1 was “Give me a healthy dinner recipe”. Both times it gave lemon chicken with roasted vegetables and quinoa, oven at 220°C. That is a fair answer. It had no way to know the dinner was vegetarian, or that the test kitchen had no oven. One run even ended: “If you tell me your calorie or protein target, or what's in your fridge, I can tailor it.”

Prompt 2 was a recipe card with six labelled lines. Both times it gave a palak paneer moong dal built from what the card listed, with grams and minutes in the steps, in about 25 to 27 minutes. It put the protein at about 34 g per serving. That number is the AI's own estimate, not verified nutrition. Each run ended with one question to make the dish better. This was a test prompt, not a cooked meal.

The six lines:
Serves: who it is for
Ingredients: what you have
Method: the shape of the answer you want
Tastes like: one example
Don't: your limits
Taste and adjust: ask it to check its own work and ask you one question

This is not a magic prompt. It is what you would tell any stranger cooking in your kitchen. Try the same six lines on an email or a study plan.
